lead.question:
let μ := Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => ProbabilityTheory.cond (Measure.count : Measure (ℤ × ℤ)) steps)
  let inc (i : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℤ × ℤ) := w i
  let peak (n : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℤ × ℤ) := (Finset.range (n+1)).sup fun i =>
    localTime inc n w (position inc i w)
  let hit (m k : ℕ) : Set (ℕ → ℤ × ℤ) := {w | ∃ n, peak n w = m ∧
    (k : ℕ∞) ≤ (favouriteSites inc n w).encard}
  ∃ G : ℕ → Set (ℕ → ℤ × ℤ), (∀ᵐ w ∂μ, ∀ᶠ m in atTop, w ∈ G m) ∧
    (∑' m : ℕ, μ (hit m 4 ∩ G m)) ≠ ∞
lead.title: Erdős Problem 1165 · step 2

review.statement: For the fixed product measure μ of independent uniform nearest-neighbour increments on ℤ², let hit(m,4) be the set of paths for which some time n has peak local time m and at least four favourite sites. The supplied target quantifies ∃ G : ℕ → Set (ℕ → ℤ × ℤ), such that for μ-almost every w there exists M(w) with w ∈ G(m) for every m ≥ M(w), and ∑′ m, μ(hit(m,4) ∩ G(m)) ≠ ∞. The supplied body has no explicit hypotheses.
review.significance: This is the summability step in the upper bound on simultaneous favourite sites for planar simple random walk. Hao, Li, Okada and Zheng prove the stronger untrimmed summability estimate in Section 4.4 of their revised paper. [arXiv v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.00995v2)
review.settlement_test: A proof of ∑′ m, μ(hit(m,4)) ≠ ∞ suffices by taking G(m) = Set.univ. The Lean task is settled by an independent kernel replay of the exact catalogue declaration, including its original imports and hypotheses, with a transitive axiom check.
review.aliases: Erdős Problem 1165, step R1.H2. Favourite sites, favorite sites, favourite points, favourite values, and most visited sites. The paper calls the positive-level event M_m^4. Erdős and Révész posed the multiplicity question in §2.1 of their 1987 paper for the walk on the line. [Original paper](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-26.pdf)

review.proof_or_witness:
Take G(m) = Set.univ for every m. The peak is positive because time zero is counted, so hit(0,4) is empty. For m ≥ 1, suppose time n witnesses hit(m,4) and take the first time j ≤ n at which four sites have local time at least m. The count starts below four and increases by at most one per step, so it is exactly four at j. The peak is monotone and is m at n, so it is also m at j. Thus j witnesses the paper’s exactly-four event M_m^4. The reverse inclusion follows directly. The events are measurable as countable unions of finite-prefix events. Hao, Li, Okada and Zheng’s Proposition 4.7 and the six-tiling cover in §4.4 give μ(hit(m,4)) ≤ C m^(−3κ), with 3κ > 1 by (4.28). The sum is finite, and membership in G(m) holds for every path and every m. [Paper, equations (2.9) and (4.28), Proposition 4.7](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.00995v2)

The pinned parent formalization credits Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol. Its structural recurrence derives the finite series for `simpleRandomWalk (levelFavoriteSet m 4)` internally at lines 701–706, before using Borel–Cantelli. The parent assembly supplies the necessary maximum lower-deviation input through `hasPlanarMaximumLowerDeviation_of_asymmetricPairSource` and the concrete pair source.
